Begin with a plane wave, $\psi(x,t)=e^{i(kx-\omega t)},$ or with its real form, $\psi(x,t)=\sin(kx-\omega t).$ A crest, a trough, or any other point of fixed phase moves so that $kx-\omega t=\text{constant}.$ Choosing the constant to be zero for convenience gives $x=\frac{\omega}{k}t,
\qquad
v_{\mathrm{phase}}=\frac{\omega}{k}.$ Since $\omega=2\pi/T$ and $k=2\pi/\lambda$, $v_{\mathrm{phase}}=\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{\lambda}{T}.$ This is just the distance by which a given phase advances during one period.

p.src: For a nonrelativistic Schrödinger wave, with $\hbar=1$, energy and momentum are $\omega$ and $k$, so $\omega(k)=\frac{k^2}{2m}.$ Its phase velocity is therefore $v_{\mathrm{phase}}=\frac{k}{2m}.$ The ordinary velocity of a particle with momentum $k$, however, is $k/m$. The factor-of-two mismatch is the first warning that the movement of a plane-wave phase is not the movement of the particle.

This can be seen directly in the wavefunction. Write a general Schrödinger field as a sum or integral of modes, $\psi(x,t)=\sum_k a_k e^{ikx}e^{-i\omega(k)t},$ with normalization factors suppressed. After the shift, $\begin{aligned}\psi(x,t)
&\longrightarrow
\sum_k a_k e^{ikx}e^{-i[\omega(k)+C]t}
\\
&=e^{-iCt}\psi(x,t).\end{aligned}$ Every mode has acquired the same time-dependent phase. The conjugate field acquires the opposite phase, and therefore $\begin{aligned}
\psi^*(x,t)\psi(x,t)
&\longrightarrow
e^{iCt}e^{-iCt}\psi^*(x,t)\psi(x,t)
\\
&=\psi^*(x,t)\psi(x,t).
\end{aligned}$ The same cancellation occurs in expectation values. A quantity that changes when the zero of energy is shifted cannot be the physical propagation speed of the Schrödinger particle. Phase velocity is therefore partly conventional.

p.src:
A localized particle is represented not by one infinite plane wave but by a packet. The component waves add constructively in the region of the packet and destructively outside it. The motion of this pattern can already be found from two nearby waves: $\psi(x,t)=
\sin(kx-\omega t)+
\sin(k'x-\omega't),$ where $k'$ is close to $k$ and $\omega'=\omega(k')$. A locus of constructive interference occurs where their phases agree, $kx-\omega t=k'x-\omega't.$ Thus $(k-k')x=(\omega-\omega')t,$ and the reinforcing pattern moves according to $x=\frac{\omega-\omega'}{k-k'}t.$ Taking the neighboring-wave limit gives $x=\frac{d\omega}{dk}t,
\qquad
v_{\mathrm{group}}=\frac{d\omega}{dk}.$ This is the velocity of the envelope—the localized lump produced by the interference of the component waves.

Set $\hbar=c_{\mathrm{light}}=1$. The relativistic relation is $E=\sqrt{p^2+m^2},
\qquad
\omega(k)=\sqrt{k^2+m^2}.$ It is useful to establish the massless case first. When $m=0$, $\omega=|k|.$ On the right-moving branch $k>0$, $\omega=k$, and therefore $v_{\mathrm{phase}}=\frac{\omega}{k}=1,
\qquad
v_{\mathrm{group}}=\frac{d\omega}{dk}=1.$ On the left-moving branch both velocities have the corresponding negative sign. In either case their speed is the speed of light. Because the dispersion relation is linear on either branch, all Fourier components on that branch move with the same velocity.

u.src: Translation Symmetry and Conservation Laws
en: Translation Symmetry and Conservation Laws
ja: 並進対称性と保存則
zh: 平移对称性与守恒定律

p.src:
The same plane-wave phases give a compact account of conservation laws. Begin with energy conservation. An annihilation field acting on an incoming particle of energy $\omega_j$ contributes a time factor $e^{-i\omega_j t},$ whereas a creation field producing an outgoing particle of energy $\omega'_r$ contributes $e^{+i\omega'_r t}.$ For several incoming and outgoing particles, their product is $\exp\!\left[
i\left(\sum_r\omega'_r-\sum_j\omega_j\right)t
\right].$ If the interaction may occur at any time with the same amplitude, the amplitude includes an integral over the interaction time: $\begin{aligned}
&\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dt\,
\exp\!\left[
i\left(\sum_r\omega'_r-\sum_j\omega_j\right)t
\right]
\\
&\quad =2\pi\,
\delta\!\left(\sum_r\omega'_r-\sum_j\omega_j\right).
\end{aligned}$ The delta function requires total outgoing energy to equal total incoming energy. Equal amplitude at every possible interaction time is time-translation invariance, and it produces energy conservation.

\right].$ 如果相互作用可以在任意时刻以相同振幅发生，则振幅包含对相互作用时间的积分： $\begin{aligned}
&\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dt\,
\exp\!\left[
i\left(\sum_r\omega'_r-\sum_j\omega_j\right)t
\right]
\\
&\quad =2\pi\,
\delta\!\left(\sum_r\omega'_r-\sum_j\omega_j\right).
\end{aligned}$ δ函数要求出射总能量等于入射总能量。在每个可能的相互作用时刻振幅都相同，就是时间平移不变性，它产生能量守恒。

Space translation gives momentum conservation by the same mechanism. Consider a physical one-to-two decay in which an incoming particle of momentum $k$ disappears and two particles of momenta $k'_1$ and $k'_2$ appear. A local interaction at position $x$ contains one annihilation field and two creation fields, $\mathcal{O}(x)=\psi^\dagger(x)\psi^\dagger(x)\psi(x).$ Suppressing time dependence and normalization, the relevant mode factors are $\begin{aligned}\psi(x)&\supset a_k e^{ikx},
\\
\psi^\dagger(x)&\supset a_{k'_1}^\dagger e^{-ik'_1x},
\qquad
\psi^\dagger(x)\supset a_{k'_2}^\dagger e^{-ik'_2x}.\end{aligned}$ In the matrix element $\langle k'_1,k'_2|\mathcal{O}(x)|k\rangle,$ the annihilation operator removes the incoming particle and the two creation operators supply the outgoing particles. Once those operator actions are taken, the position-dependent factor that remains is $e^{-ik'_1x}e^{-ik'_2x}e^{ikx}
=e^{i(k-k'_1-k'_2)x}.$ Because no position is privileged, one integrates over all possible decay positions: $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}dx\,
e^{i(k-k'_1-k'_2)x}
=2\pi\delta(k-k'_1-k'_2).$ The surviving amplitude therefore obeys $k=k'_1+k'_2.$ In three dimensions the same calculation uses $d^3x$, bold momentum vectors, and a three-dimensional delta function. Nothing in the argument depends on having only one incoming particle or two outgoing particles. For arbitrary particle numbers, integration over the common interaction position produces $\delta^{(3)}\!\left(
\sum_j\mathbf{k}_j-\sum_r\mathbf{k}'_r
\right).$ Equal amplitude at every position is spatial translation invariance, and it gives momentum conservation just as equal amplitude at every time gives energy conservation.

p.src: Bosons permit any nonnegative occupation number in a one-particle state, and their creation-operator algebra actually favors an already occupied state. For one bosonic mode, the normalized number-state convention writes the occupation enhancement as (The lecture states the square-root occupation enhancement; this indexed equation is its standard number-state form.)  $a^\dagger|n\rangle=\sqrt{n+1}\,|n+1\rangle.$ Suppose an excited atom can emit a photon into many possible modes. In the absence of other photons, the different directions and momenta occur with their ordinary probability distribution. If a particular mode already contains many photons—all with the same momentum, energy, and frequency—emission into that mode is enhanced by the corresponding square-root occupation factor. The atom preferentially adds its photon to the state already populated. This is stimulated emission and is a concrete expression of bosonic congregation.

Focus on a single one-particle state. It is either empty, $|0\rangle$, or occupied, $|1\rangle$. Creation and annihilation act as $\begin{aligned}A^\dagger|0\rangle&=|1\rangle,
&
A^\dagger|1\rangle&=0,
\\
A|0\rangle&=0,
&
A|1\rangle&=|0\rangle.\end{aligned}$ The unadorned zero on the right is the zero vector, not the empty state $|0\rangle$. Attempting to add a second fermion does not return the vacuum; it returns no physical state at all.

The harmonic oscillator makes the distinction concrete. Its ground state, the state with no oscillator excitation, has a Gaussian wavefunction such as $\phi_0(q)\propto e^{-\alpha q^2},
\qquad \alpha>0.$ This is a perfectly good, normalizable state. By contrast, $\phi(q)\equiv0$ is the zero vector: it has no probability amplitude anywhere and is not a state. Thus $A^\dagger|1\rangle=0$ says that the attempted second creation produces the zero vector.

Adopting that notation, the single-mode rules are $\begin{aligned}c^\dagger|0\rangle&=|1\rangle,
&c^\dagger|1\rangle&=0,
\\
c|0\rangle&=0,
&c|1\rangle&=|0\rangle.\end{aligned}$ Now evaluate the two possible products on both basis states. On the empty state, $\begin{aligned}c^\dagger c|0\rangle&=0,
&
cc^\dagger|0\rangle&=|0\rangle.\end{aligned}$ On the occupied state, $\begin{aligned}c^\dagger c|1\rangle&=|1\rangle,
&
cc^\dagger|1\rangle&=0.\end{aligned}$ Their sum returns whichever state it acts on: $\begin{aligned}(c^\dagger c+cc^\dagger)|0\rangle&=|0\rangle,
\\
(c^\dagger c+cc^\dagger)|1\rangle&=|1\rangle.\end{aligned}$ Since $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ span the one-mode state space, $c^\dagger c+cc^\dagger=1.$ The plus-sign combination is the anticommutator, $\{A,B\}=AB+BA,$ so the fermionic relation is $\{c,c^\dagger\}=1.$ It is the fermionic analog of the bosonic commutator $[a,a^\dagger]=aa^\dagger-a^\dagger a=1.$

p.src:
The momentum-labeled algebra first says that two identical fermions of the same species cannot occupy one momentum mode. It says more. A particle localized at position $x$ is created by $\psi^\dagger(x)=\sum_k c_k^\dagger e^{-ikx},$ up to normalization. At the origin, trying to create two particles gives $\begin{aligned}\psi^\dagger(0)\psi^\dagger(0)|\Omega\rangle
&=\sum_{k,k'}c_k^\dagger c_{k'}^\dagger|\Omega\rangle.\end{aligned}$ The labels $k$ and $k'$ are dummy summation variables. Interchanging them leaves the double sum unchanged, so it may be averaged with its relabeled form: $\begin{aligned}\sum_{k,k'}c_k^\dagger c_{k'}^\dagger|\Omega\rangle
&=\frac12\sum_{k,k'}
\left(c_k^\dagger c_{k'}^\dagger
+c_{k'}^\dagger c_k^\dagger\right)|\Omega\rangle
\\
&=\frac12\sum_{k,k'}
\{c_k^\dagger,c_{k'}^\dagger\}|\Omega\rangle
=0.\end{aligned}$

p.src:
Let $|N\rangle$ and $|C\rangle$ be orthonormal states localized in Nevada and Connecticut. Then $|+\rangle=\frac{|N\rangle+|C\rangle}{\sqrt2},
\qquad
|-\rangle=\frac{|N\rangle-|C\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$ The state $|+\rangle$ gives equal probabilities of finding its one electron in Nevada or Connecticut. The state $|-\rangle$ gives the same position probabilities but differs by a relative phase. The two states are orthogonal: $\langle+|-\rangle=0.$ Two electrons cannot both occupy $|+\rangle$, and they cannot both occupy $|-\rangle$, but exclusion does not prevent one electron from occupying each state.

Consider particles confined to a finite three-dimensional box of side $L$, with periodic boundary conditions. In one dimension the allowed wave numbers are $k=\frac{2\pi n}{L},

\qquad n_x,n_y,n_z\in\mathbb{Z}.$ The allowed momentum vectors therefore form a lattice in momentum space. This is not a lattice of positions; each point labels an allowed momentum state. Increasing $L$ decreases the separation $2\pi/L$ between neighboring values, while the lattice continues without bound in every momentum direction.

It does not localize any one boson at a particular position; each boson is correspondingly uncertain about where it is. When the occupation becomes large, the common wavefunction builds up a macroscopic field amplitude, and the field behaves increasingly like a classical field.

After those states are occupied, further particles must enter successive shells.

p.src: Because the energy is proportional to the squared distance from the origin in momentum space, minimizing the total energy means packing the occupied points as closely around $\mathbf{k}=0$ as exclusion permits. With many fermions the occupied region approximates a sphere. Its boundary is the Fermi surface, its interior is the Fermi sea, and the complete filled region is the Fermi sphere. At finite volume the boundary is slightly jagged because the available points form a lattice, but this detail becomes negligible for a large system.

p.src: The fermionic ground state has much more energy than the corresponding bosonic ground state. All the bosons can remain at zero momentum, but most of the fermions are forced into nonzero-momentum states. As more fermions are added, the maximum occupied momentum grows. Moreover, a shell at large momentum contains more lattice points than a shell near the origin. A large Fermi sphere therefore contains many particles at substantial momentum and only a small number in the lowest-momentum states.

ja: フェルミオン基底状態は、対応するボース基底状態よりもはるかに多くのエネルギーを持つ。すべてのボース粒子はゼロ運動量にとどまることができるが、フェルミ粒子の大部分は非零運動量状態へと強いられる。フェルミ粒子がさらに加えられると、占められる最大運動量が増大する。さらに、大きな運動量の殻は原点近くの殻よりも多くの格子点を含む。したがって大きなフェルミ球は、かなりの運動量を持つ多数の粒子を含み、最低運動量状態には少数の粒子しか含まない。
zh: 费米子基态的能量比相应的玻色子基态高得多。所有玻色子都可以留在零动量处，但大多数费米子被迫进入非零动量态。随着加入的费米子越来越多，被占据的最大动量也随之增大。此外，大动量处的壳层比原点附近的壳层包含更多的点阵点。因此，一个大的费米球中包含许多处于可观动量的粒子，而只有少数粒子处于最低动量态。

p.src: The contrast continues in the excited states. For bosons, the first excitation is obtained by removing any one boson from the condensate and placing it in a first excited one-particle state: $(N,0,0,\ldots)\longrightarrow (N-1,1,0,\ldots).$ It makes no difference which boson is moved; the particles are identical. Higher excitations can be made in several ways. Depending on the level spacing, one may place one boson in a higher level or place two bosons in the first excited level. Exciting the bosonic system means promoting particles out of the condensate into higher-energy states.

ja.text: この対比は励起状態でも続く。ボース粒子の場合、最初の励起は任意の一つのボース粒子を凝縮体から取り除き、それを第一励起一粒子状態に置くことによって得られる：
どのボース粒子を動かすかは違いを生まない。粒子は同一である。より高い励起はいくつかの方法で作ることができる。準位間隔に応じて、一つのボース粒子をより高い準位に置くか、二つのボース粒子を第一励起準位に置くことができる。ボース系を励起することは、粒子を凝縮体からより高いエネルギー状態へと昇進させることを意味する。

zh.text: 这种对比在激发态中继续存在。对于玻色子，第一激发态是通过从凝聚体中取出任意一个玻色子，并将其放入第一激发单粒子态而得到的：
移动的是哪一个玻色子并无区别；粒子是全同的。更高的激发可以通过几种方式产生。取决于能级间距，可以把一个玻色子放入更高的能级，也可以把两个玻色子放入第一激发能级。激发玻色子系统意味着把粒子从凝聚体中提升到更高能量的态。

p.src: For fermions, no particle can be moved to another point inside the filled Fermi sphere, because every such point is already occupied. Taking a fermion from deep inside the sea and placing it above the surface is possible, but it costs a large amount of energy. The least expensive excitation takes a fermion from just inside the Fermi surface and moves it to an unoccupied state just outside. The promoted electron has only a small energy above the surface, and the vacant state left behind lies only a small energy below it.

p.src: An electron above the Fermi surface may later drop into an available hole. Its energy then decreases, so radiation must carry the released energy away. One may describe the event as an electron dropping to an unoccupied lower state and emitting one or more photons. Equivalently, one may say that an electron and a hole annihilate into radiation. The hole is not an additional fundamental constituent of the box; it is an absence in the filled many-electron state. Nevertheless, its energy and charge make it useful to treat it as a particle-like excitation.

ja: フェルミ面より上の電子は、後に空いている正孔へ落ち込むことがある。そのときそのエネルギーは減少するので、放出されたエネルギーを放射が運び去らなければならない。この事象は、電子が空いている低い状態へ落ち込み、一つ以上の光子を放出すると記述できる。等価に、電子と正孔が対消滅して放射になると言うこともできる。正孔は箱の追加の基本的構成要素ではなく、満たされた多電子状態における欠如である。それにもかかわらず、そのエネルギーと電荷のため、粒子のような励起として扱うと便利である。
zh: 费米面以上的电子随后可能落入一个可用的空穴。此时其能量降低，因此辐射必须将释放的能量带走。人们可以将该事件描述为一个电子落入一个未被占据的较低能态并发射一个或多个光子。等价地，也可以说一个电子和一个空穴湮灭为辐射。空穴并不是盒中额外的基本组分；它是被填充的多电子态中的一个缺失。尽管如此，它的能量和电荷使得将其视为一种类粒子激发是有用的。

p.src: (Lecture timestamp: 01:36:52)  Question from the audience: Does promoting an electron mean moving it from one lattice point to another in momentum space?

u.src: (Lecture timestamp: 01:36:52)  Question from the audience: Does promoting an electron mean moving it from one lattice point to another in momentum space?

ja: (講義時刻: 01:36:52)  受講者からの質問: 電子を励起するとは、運動量空間のある格子点から別の格子点へ動かすことを意味するのか？
zh: (讲课时间: 01:36:52)  听众提问: 激发一个电子是否意味着在动量空间中将其从一个格点移动到另一个格点？

p.src: Response: It means moving the electron from one energy level to another. For free particles in the box, the momentum lattice labels those levels, but the same idea does not depend on a momentum-space lattice. In an atom the positive charge is concentrated in the nucleus. Electrons fill the lowest available atomic levels, and a photon can promote one electron to an excited level, leaving a vacancy in the level from which it came. That vacancy is the atomic counterpart of a hole.

ja: 回答: それは電子をあるエネルギー準位から別のエネルギー準位へ動かすことを意味する。箱の中の自由粒子では、運動量格子がそれらの準位をラベル付けするが、同じ考えは運動量空間の格子に依存しない。原子では、正電荷は原子核に集中している。電子は利用可能な最も低い原子準位を満たし、光子は一つの電子を励起準位へ上げ、それが来た準位に空席を残すことができる。その空席が正孔の原子的対応物である。
zh: 回答: 它意味着将电子从一个能级移动到另一个能级。对于盒中的自由粒子，动量点阵标记这些能级，但同样的想法并不依赖于动量空间点阵。在原子中，正电荷集中在原子核内。电子填充最低的可用原子能级，而一个光子可以将一个电子激发到激发能级，并在其原来所在的能级中留下一个空位。该空位就是空穴在原子中的对应物。

p.src: In the box, photon absorption likewise converts the photon energy into an electron above the Fermi surface and a hole below it. In an atom, the same language describes the excited electron together with the vacancy left among the occupied lower levels.

zh: 在盒中，光子吸收同样将光子能量转化为费米面以上的一个电子和其下方的一个空穴。在原子中，同样的语言描述被激发的电子以及在被占据的较低能级中留下的空位。

p.src: (Lecture timestamp: 01:39:16)  Question from the audience: Can a low-energy photon be absorbed by an electron anywhere in the Fermi sphere?

u.src: (Lecture timestamp: 01:39:16)  Question from the audience: Can a low-energy photon be absorbed by an electron anywhere in the Fermi sphere?
en: (Lecture timestamp: 01:39:16)  Question from the audience: Can a low-energy photon be absorbed by an electron anywhere in the Fermi sphere?
ja: (講義時刻: 01:39:16)  受講者からの質問: 低エネルギーの光子はフェルミ球内のどこにある電子にも吸収されうるか？
zh: (讲课时间: 01:39:16)  听众提问: 低能光子能否被费米球中任意位置的电子吸收？

p.src: Response: No. If the electron lies deep in the Fermi sea, every nearby state is already occupied, and a low-energy photon cannot lift it all the way to an unoccupied state above the surface. Only electrons close enough to the Fermi surface have accessible empty states within the photon’s energy range. A sufficiently energetic photon can excite an electron from deep in the sea.

ja: 回答: いいえ。電子がフェルミ海の深くにあるなら、近くのすべての状態はすでに占有されており、低エネルギーの光子はそれを表面より上の空いている状態まで持ち上げることはできない。光子のエネルギー範囲内で到達可能な空状態を持つのは、フェルミ面に十分近い電子だけである。十分にエネルギーの高い光子は、海の深くから電子を励起できる。
zh: 回答: 不能。如果电子位于费米海深处，其附近的所有态都已被占据，低能光子无法将其一直提升到费米面以上的未占据态。只有足够靠近费米面的电子，才在光子能量范围内具有可及的空态。能量足够高的光子可以将电子从费米海深处激发出来。

p.src: The low-energy absorption cross section is therefore controlled by the surface of the Fermi sea rather than by its whole volume. Electrons deep in the sea are blocked from making small transitions; electrons just below the surface can be moved just above it.

ja: したがって、低エネルギー吸収断面積はフェルミ海の全体積ではなく、その表面によって支配される。海の深くの電子は小さな遷移を行うことを妨げられ、表面のすぐ下の電子はそのすぐ上へ動かされうる。
zh: 因此，低能吸收截面由费米海的表面而非其整个体积决定。费米海深处的电子被阻止发生小跃迁；而紧邻费米面下方的电子则可以被移动到紧邻其上方。

ja: (講義時刻: 01:40:42)  受講者からの質問: 入射光子なしで、電子が互いに直接相互作用することを何が妨げるのか？
zh: (讲课时间: 01:40:42)  听众提问: 是什么阻止了电子在没有入射光子的情况下直接相互作用？

p.src: Response: Nothing. Electron–electron interactions are being neglected in this simple model, because including them makes the Fermi-sea picture more complicated. In this first approximation to a metal, their effective influence is treated as weak enough that it can usually be ignored.

u.src: Response: Nothing. Electron–electron interactions are being neglected in this simple model, because including them makes the Fermi-sea picture more complicated. In this first approximation to a metal, their effective influence is treated as weak enough that it can usually be ignored.

zh: 回答: 没有任何东西。在这个简单模型中，电子–电子相互作用被忽略，因为将其包括进来会使费米海图像变得更加复杂。在对金属的这一初步近似中，它们的有效影响被视为足够弱，以至于通常可以忽略。

ja: (講義時刻: 01:41:10)  受講者からの質問: 一つの光子が複数の電子を励起するのに十分なエネルギーを運ぶとどうなるか？
zh: (讲课时间: 01:41:10)  听众提问: 如果一个光子携带足够的能量来激发多个电子，会发生什么？

p.src: Response: Any process consistent with the conservation laws is possible in principle. The photon can create more than one electron–hole pair: exciting two electrons also leaves two holes. Such a process creates more excitations and is generally less probable than using the energy to excite one electron much more strongly.

ja: 回答: 保存則と整合するいかなる過程も原理的には可能である。光子は複数の電子–正孔対を生成できる：二つの電子を励起すれば二つの正孔も残る。そのような過程はより多くの励起を生成し、一般に、エネルギーを一つの電子をはるかに強く励起するために使う場合よりも確率が低い。

p.src: (Lecture timestamp: 01:42:06)  Question from the audience: Can two photons be absorbed together when neither photon alone can produce the excitation?

ja: (講義時刻: 01:42:06)  受講者からの質問: どちらの光子も単独では励起を生成できないとき、二つの光子が一緒に吸収されうるか？

p.src: Response: Yes. Absorption is probabilistic, and a two-photon process can occur when the combined photon energy reaches an available excitation even though either photon separately falls below the required energy. If the available light carries too little energy to reach any allowed excitation, it largely passes through the system.

u.src: Response: Yes. Absorption is probabilistic, and a two-photon process can occur when the combined photon energy reaches an available excitation even though either photon separately falls below the required energy. ja: 回答: はい。吸収は確率的であり、二光子過程は、それぞれの光子が単独では必要なエネルギーを下回っていても、合わせた光子エネルギーが利用可能な励起に達するときに起こりうる。利用可能な光が許された励起に達するにはエネルギーが小さすぎる場合、それは主に系を通過する。

zh: (讲课时间: 01:43:49)  听众提问: 为什么电子–电子相互作用被称为弱相互作用，尽管所有电子都带相同的负电荷？

p.src: Response: The electrons are immersed in the compensating positive background. That background screens the charge of an electron and reduces the effective interaction in this simplified setting. The interaction is not absent; treating it requires the screening response of the medium.

u.src: Response: The electrons are immersed in the compensating positive background. That background screens the charge of an electron and reduces the effective interaction in this simplified setting. The interaction is not absent; treating it requires the screening response of the medium.
en: Response: The electrons are immersed in the compensating positive background. That background screens the charge of an electron and reduces the effective interaction in this simplified setting. The interaction is not absent; treating it requires the screening response of the medium.
ja: 回答: 電子は補償する正の背景の中に浸されている。その背景が電子の電荷を遮蔽し、この簡略化された設定における有効相互作用を弱める。相互作用が存在しないわけではなく、それを扱うには媒質の遮蔽応答が必要である。
zh: 回答: 电子浸没在起补偿作用的正电荷背景中。该背景屏蔽了电子的电荷，并在这个简化设定中减弱了有效相互作用。相互作用并非不存在；处理它需要考虑介质的屏蔽响应。

ja: 通常の空の真空は、そのような理論の基底状態にはなり得ない。正エネルギーのフェルミオンは光子を放出してより低い状態へ落ち込むことができる。ゼロで止まることを強制するものは何もない。負エネルギーの状態へと進み続け、さらに多くの放射を放出し、際限なく落ち込むことができる。フェルミオンが失ったエネルギーは放射場に現れるであろう。したがって、下に有界でないスペクトルは安定な通常の真空を与えない。
zh: 普通的空真空不可能是这种理论的基态。一个正能量费米子可以辐射一个光子并跃迁到更低的状态。没有什么会迫使它在零处停下：它可以继续进入负能量态，发射更多辐射，并无限制地向下跃迁。费米子失去的能量会出现在辐射场中。因此，一个下方无界的谱不会给出稳定的普通真空。

p.src: Fermionic exclusion supplies a different starting point. Fill every negative-energy one-particle state, up to zero energy, with one fermion. No further fermion can fall into those states because each is already occupied. Adding another negative-energy fermion is impossible, while adding a positive-energy fermion raises the energy. The completely filled negative-energy sea can therefore be taken as the many-body ground state and called the vacuum.

This is the basic particle–antiparticle interpretation to which the negative-energy spectrum led.

p.src:
The same rescue cannot be applied to bosons. A bosonic state admits arbitrarily many particles, so there is no way to fill a negative-energy level once and block further occupation. More bosons could always be added to that level, lowering the energy again and again: $\begin{aligned}
\text{fermionic mode: }&n=0\ \text{or}\ 1,\\
\text{bosonic mode: }&n=0,1,2,\ldots .
\end{aligned}$ The proposed bosonic system would still have no ground state. In this elementary construction, the stability of the filled sea depends precisely on fermionic exclusion.

\text{fermionic mode: }&n=0\ \text{or}\ 1,\\
\text{bosonic mode: }&n=0,1,2,\ldots .
\end{aligned}$ The proposed bosonic system would still have no ground state. In this elementary construction, the stability of the filled sea depends precisely on fermionic exclusion.
